find.label: Find a character
find.placeholder: A Tangut character or text, a code, a reading, a meaning, U+17000…
find.door.cangjie: Type the glyph code letter by letter; candidates are numbered for quick entry. The keyboard is also the key chart, and every component has its own code.
find.door.reading: Type a reconstruction in any of eight systems. Candidates show which system reads them so.
find.door.draw: Sketch the character and scan the glyphs closest in shape. The match is rough; expect to look down the list.
find.door.parts: Pick the components you can see; each pick narrows the characters and the remaining parts.
find.tip: Reading a text? Paste a line of Tangut above: each character is listed with its meaning and reading.
find.none: Nothing in the records matches {text}. The meanings are in English, Japanese and Chinese; readings may be typed without diacritics.
cangjie.label: Cangjie code
cangjie.noCode: No code begins with {code}. Backspace and try another letter; the keyboard dims the keys that lead nowhere.
cangjie.keys: <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>1</kbd>–<kbd>9</kbd> adds a candidate to the text · <kbd>←</kbd><kbd>→</kbd> highlight · <kbd>↑</kbd><kbd>↓</kbd> page · <kbd>Esc</kbd> clears · <kbd>⌫</kbd> on an empty box deletes from the text
cangjie.keysHint: Each key and the shapes it names. Faint keys continue no code.
cangjie.keysHintIdle: Each key and the shapes it names.
cangjie.componentsHint: Each component is typed as p and its own code.
sijiao.label: Four-corner code
sijiao.keys: Six digits, read from the four corners: <kbd>Space</kbd> adds the highlighted candidate · <kbd>←</kbd><kbd>→</kbd> highlight · <kbd>↑</kbd><kbd>↓</kbd> page · <kbd>Esc</kbd> clears
sijiao.digitsHint: The letter each digit is typed on.
sijiao.cornersHint: The first four digits read the top left, top right, bottom left and bottom right corner; the fifth the shape above the bottom right; the sixth the rest. Codes are from 韓小忙 (2021), through Tangut-rhyme-dictionaries-data; {count} characters carry one.
reading.intro: Type a reconstruction in any system: Li Fanwen, Gong, Gong Xun, Arakawa, Miyake, Nishida, Kychanov or Sofronov. Diacritics and IPA are optional; ɨ can be typed i, ś as s, ŋ as ng.
reading.label: Reconstruction
reading.placeholder: a reading, e.g. ndzi or dzjɨ1
reading.none: No reading in {systems} comes close to {query}{tone}. Try fewer letters, or drop the tone.
reading.cut: The first {shown} of {total}. Add letters or a tone to narrow.
draw.intro: Draw the whole character, upright and filling the square.
draw.canvas: Drawing pad: draw a character with the mouse, a pen or a finger
draw.note: How rough this is. No recognizer for the whole Tangut script is openly available. The pad compares the line you drew and the direction it runs with the printed glyphs of five Tangut faces, and keeps each character's best place in any of them. Stroke order plays no part. On eighty characters drawn by one reader, with the stroke count weighed as it is by default, the right character came first about three times in ten and within the first five about one time in two. Expect to scan the list, and reach for Cangjie or a reading when you have one.
draw.failed: The glyph shapes could not be loaded.
draw.keys: <kbd>Enter</kbd> adds the first and clears the pad · <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> undoes a stroke · <kbd>Esc</kbd> clears
draw.empty: The closest glyphs appear here after the first stroke and change with every stroke after it.
parts.intro: Choose the components you can see in the character. Each choice keeps only the characters built with it, and the palette keeps only the parts that still occur.
parts.noneChosen: No parts chosen yet: pick from the palette below.
parts.noMatch: No recorded description holds all of these parts. Remove one to widen the search.
parts.noMatchLayout: No recorded description holds all of these parts in that layout. Remove one to widen the search.
parts.empty: The characters built from the chosen parts appear here.
writing.label: Your text
attest.title: In a text
attest.absent: Not yet recorded. The corpus so far is one chapter of the Tangut Bodhicaryāvatāra ({characters} characters, {distinct} distinct), so most characters have no attestation here yet.
card.label: Character
card.blank: Pick a character to see its record here, with ways to copy it or add it to your text.
card.blankKeys: Arrow keys move through candidates; <kbd>Enter</kbd> adds the highlighted one.
card.isComponent: A component: it is a part of other characters, not built from parts itself.
card.noDescription: No description from parts is recorded for this character.
card.credit: Meanings, readings and descriptions: Open Tangut (MIT), from CCAMC and Wiktionary. Codes: RIME Tangut Cangjie, whose table warns that some codes are wrong.
about.lead: Everything the site shows is read from static files built from the works below. The text you write stays in this browser. Every drawing and every character you pick is recorded, as the last section says.
about.how: How the finders read the records
about.code: The site’s code is MIT. Source:
find.door.sijiao: Type the six digits of the four-corner code; candidates are numbered for quick entry. The number pad is also the key chart.
meaning.intro: Search what a character means. Every meaning is recorded in English, Japanese and Chinese, so a word in any of the three finds the characters it glosses; a gloss with several senses is searched sense by sense.
meaning.label: Search by meaning
meaning.none: No meaning in the records holds “{query}”.
meaning.cut: The first {shown} of {total}; narrow the word to see the rest.
parts.splitTitle: Break {part} into the parts it is built from
fanqie.intro: Type the two characters a fanqie is spelt with — the upper, which gives the initial, and then the lower, which gives the rhyme — and the characters they spell appear. One character finds every character whose spelling uses it.
fanqie.label: Fanqie characters
fanqie.none: No character in the rhyme books is spelt with “{text}”.
nav.chart.hint: Read the rhyme books as a chart
chart.intro: The 文海 as a chart: each row is a rhyme with its tone, each column an initial group, and every character stands in the cell where the two meet. Hover a character for its fanqie, its sound gloss and its meaning.
chart.legend: The 105 rhymes and nine initial groups are the rhyme books’ own; the crossings are read from the 同音 and 文海 tables. Tibetan transcriptions are not recorded in this data, so the cells hold the characters, their fanqie and the Chinese sound gloss.
fanqie.inferred: No source gives this character a reading; inferred from the spelling it shares with {char}.
card.posSource: Marked in the Chinese gloss; the source’s own classification.
fanqie.hint: Choose the upper character first, then the lower.
chart.soundIntro: The {sounds} sounds the glosses record, each with the characters that sound so and the fanqie written for them. A character can stand under more than one sound.
about.openTangut: Open Tangut by imlooh (MIT), a dictionary of the Tangut block in English, Japanese and Chinese scraped from CCAMC and Wiktionary. 6,144 entries, each with readings in Li Fanwen 2008, Gong Hwang-cherng, Gong Xun 2024-11, Arakawa Shintarō, Miyake, Nishida 1966, Kychanov 2006 and Sofronov 1968, and sound glosses after Li Fanwen and Nie Lishan. The 文海 gloss is present for few entries.
about.cangjieSource: rime_tangutcjkk by Hulenkius, the Tangut Cangjie scheme of Kawasaki Keigo (2016) for RIME: 11,805 full and short codes, components under codes beginning p. The table itself warns that some characters are wrongly encoded, and the repository states no licence. This is the repository’s 2026.02.02 revision: 4,725 of its 7,058 characters carry more than one code, because a glyph can be analysed more than one way, and every code is accepted and shown. A proposal to standardise the analyses that disagree with each other is still open upstream, so 250 characters hold no code that their parts alone would predict. Tutorial and practice tables: tlistlil.github.io/sps/Tang/cj.
about.rhymeBooks: Tangut-rhyme-dictionaries-data (西夏語韻書データ) by nkay0: each character’s rhyme class in the 文海, its tone, its initial group, and the two characters its fanqie is spelt from, taken from Han Xiaomang (2021) and the editions of the 文海, 文海寶韻, 同音 and 合編. The table’s own page and index numbers are not reproduced. The repository states no licence.
about.pronunciationCheck: The readings are Open Tangut’s. Their GX202411 column was compared with Xun Gong’s Tangut Pronunciation Database (2025): once its superscript tones are folded to digits, 5,743 of 6,031 readings agree, 88 differ and 58 characters are absent there.
about.strokes: Ideographs from Unicode’s TangutSources.txt (Unicode 18.0); components counted from their glyphs in this project’s review.
about.attestation: Kirill Solonin and Shintaro Arakawa, Śāntideva’s Bodhicaryāvatāra in Tangut Translation, vol. 1 (ILCAA, TUFS, 2024), CC BY 4.0: chapter 2, the manuscript IOM RAS Tangut no. 781, with the edition’s English translation and facsimile. The facsimile reproduces photographs by the Institute of Ethnology, CASS. Line readings: ぶんぽ, 西夏語公開自主ゼミ (note.com, 2024-12-30 to 2025-09-15), linked line by line and not reproduced. Lines, character boxes and crops recorded by Glyph Atlas.
about.glyphs: Noto Serif Tangut (SIL OFL 1.1), from Google Fonts. The drawing pad’s glyph masks are rendered from the same font. Descriptions use a 2 KB subset of GenZui Sans for the sixteen ideographic description characters (SIL OFL 1.1).
about.howCangjie: A typed code lists every character whose full or short code begins with it: an exact code first, then shorter codes. Wrong codes in the table are found as the table has them.
about.howReading: Readings in all eight systems are folded to plain letters: diacritics dropped, IPA letters replaced by the nearest Latin letter (ɨ ɪ → i, ə → e, ŋ → ng), separators removed. A final digit is the tone. Near matches also ignore medial j and y and a prenasal before a stop.
about.howDraw: The drawing and each glyph are stretched into the same 32-pixel square, the glyph reduced to a one-cell line along its pen, and compared by how far each line lies from the other’s and by the direction the ink runs at each point. Stroke order plays no part. On eighty characters drawn by one reader, the right character came first about three times in ten and within the first five about one time in two.
about.howParts: A character matches when its description holds every chosen part, as often as chosen. Descriptions are Open Tangut’s and use components only.
about.howAttest: A character outside the corpus has no attestation yet: the corpus is one chapter, and absence says nothing about the character.
about.markText: 𘅤 (U+18164), glossed “to write” in Open Tangut, read rjar¹ by Li Fanwen.
about.kept: Every drawing made on the Draw page and every character picked from a finder is recorded with the finder it came from, the character chosen and the place it stood in the list. A drawing kept with a pick is one example the search could be measured or trained on. A record carries a random id that lives in your browser, never your address, and there is no account. The quiz saves the same fields for each round, with the prompt it asked for.
about.footer: Descriptions are also composed in the IDS Workshop, which runs on the same component data; its data notes give each file’s source and licence.
nav.transcribe.hint: Paste a line and read it character by character
transcribe.intro: Paste or type Tangut text. Every character appears with the reading your chosen system gives it, its rhyme and its meaning, and the line can be copied as readings or as a table of all eight systems.
transcribe.empty: Type or paste Tangut text above; the readings appear here.
